original_text: –Lens–Focal length is fixed (unchangeable)–To focus the image, the distance from the lens to the object is changed–To magnify the image, the lens is                                  replaced with one having a different                                 focal length–Different lenses have different purposes–Condenser –Gathers ER from source onto specimen–Objective(s)–Gathers ER from sample to and focuses to detector; can be multiple–Intermediate and Projector –Not always found. Used to increase magnification–Called compound microscope because multiple lenses compound, or multiply the magnifying power of the unit.
explanation: This slide explains that a lens has a fixed, unchangeable focal length. To bring an image into focus, the distance between the lens and the object must be adjusted. To magnify the image, the lens is replaced with one that has a different focal length. Lenses are classified by function: 1) the Condenser gathers electromagnetic radiation (ER) from the source and focuses it onto the specimen, 2) the Objective lens (or lenses) gathers ER from the sample and focuses it toward the detector, and 3) Intermediate and Projector lenses (which are not always present) are used to further increase magnification. The instrument is called a compound microscope because multiple lenses compound, or multiply, the total magnifying power.

questions.q: Since the focal length of a lens is fixed, how is a microscope image focused?
opts: By changing the distance from the lens to the object
By adding more dyes to the specimen
By replacing the eyepiece with a camera

questions.q: What is the function of the condenser lens?
opts: It gathers electromagnetic radiation from the source and concentrates it onto the specimen.
It increases the resolution of the detector.
It holds the slide in place on the stage.
